thread.title: Investors Go Bargain Hunting With Techs on Sale

author: investopedia.com
title: Investors Go Bargain Hunting With Techs on Sale
text:
Many investors have scooped up tech stocks in recent days amid a broader global market selloff, and for good reason. Bulls on the Street have highlighted the recent dip as a prime opportunity to get into the once-red hot industry at a slightly cheaper price, recommending stocks such as Apple Inc. ( AAPL ), Alphabet Inc. ( GOOGL ), Square Inc. ( SQ ) and Microsoft Corp. ( MSFT ).
Take Advantage, Say Tech Bulls While bears warn on tech's inflated valuations, pointing to the 38% average annual return that the FAANGs have posted since 2014, Barron's highlights the fact that historically, they remain relatively inexpensive. A year following the last tech bubble in 2000, tech stocks traded at a 200% premium to the market, compared to the 30% premium shares of tech companies trade at currently. (For more, see also: The Bullish Case for Tech Stocks .)
This holds true for even the most well-known of the tech titans, including the FAANGs. Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) and Amazon Inc. ( AMZN ) are the priciest among the group, but they are also posting the strongest growth and are viewed as possessing the greatest opportunity to disrupt massive markets.
Tech Stocks Selling At Discounted Prices
Company % Off 52-Week High Amazon -14.1 Square -27.1% Microsoft -7.4% Apple -7% Alphabet -14.6% On Friday, Macquarie Securities analyst Sarah Hindlian upgraded shares of legacy IT giant Microsoft to outperform. “We are taking advantage of the market pullback...to correct our rating on Microsoft, a name we have sorely missed,” wrote Hindlian.
Canaccord Genuity analyst Michael Graham offered a similarly upbeat outlook in his reassessment of Jack Dorsey's fintech leader Square, increasing his rating on the stock from hold to buy.
“Having been on the wrong side of Square stock for some time, we believe the recent sharp selloff creates a long-term opportunity,” he wrote.
Apple has also been highlighted as an attractive buy as the smartphone maker transitions to rely more on software and services and benefits from higher ASPs and margins on its latest devices. In an interview with CNBC's "Trading Nation" on Thursday, Piper Jaffray's chief market technician Craig Johnson pointed to Apple's chart, stating that "the charts are not broken," but rather "seeing corrections in the longer-term uptrends." He added that the Microsoft is demonstrating a similar pattern. (For more, see also: 4 Best Tech Stocks to Own in 2018: Fortune .)
Moving Forward Moving forward, investors will be closely watching third quarter earnings to see if America's tech titans deliver strong enough results to outweigh negative headwinds such as rising rates, tariff threats and new regulation on the sector.
RBC Capital Markets strategist Lori Calvasina voiced concerns about the dominance of tech, writing that "we worry about tech getting hit harder in a risk-off environment because its very-over-owned by funds."
Despite the downside risk, bulls are overall confident that fundamentals will continue to carry U.S. tech titans to outperform the broader market, making the recent downturn a steal for the value investor.
